title: Unconfigured non-18-decimal token is silently treated as 18-dec 1:1 (fail-open default) — one forgotten setTokenConfig lets any NFT holder drain that strategy's full yield for ~0 payment, or bricks all claims
plausibility: Top-of-band Medium. Plausible-High dissent recorded for the severity-auditor (see severityDispute).
description: claim() prices payment by normalizing each strategy's skimmed underlying to 18 decimals (L489 _normalizeAmount), summing, discounting (L497), then denormalizing to reward-token decimals (L498 _denormalizeAmount). Both _normalizeAmount (L586-609, fallback L591 `return amount;`) and _denormalizeAmount (L617-640, fallback L622) treat an UNCONFIGURED token (tokenConfigs[token].decimals == 0 && normalizedExchangeRate == 0, the default struct state) as an 18-decimal 1:1 passthrough. Nothing links registration/funding to a required config: addYieldStrategy(strategy, token) (L227-236) takes no decimals argument and never requires a TokenConfig, and setRewardToken(_rewardToken) (L360-363) never requires a config. The decimal is set in a SEPARATE, easy-to-forget owner call (setTokenConfig, L280-287). If a registered strategy's underlying (or the reward token) is left unconfigured while it is NOT actually 18-dec (e.g. 6-dec USDC/USDT), the 18-dec passthrough mis-scales value by 10**(18-actualDecimals) (~1e12 for 6-dec stables). This is the in-scope NON-OBVIOUS owner FOOTGUN (Law 3) enabling a Law-1 value-extraction exploit — explicitly NOT the suppressed malicious-owner C-01 framing (needs no malice, just a forgotten setter).
impact: DRAIN direction (unconfigured strategy token): 100% of an unconfigured <18-decimal strategy's accrued, skimmed yield (the surplus owed to phlimbo / Limbo stakers) is delivered in full to any NFT holder for ZERO reward-token payment, repeatable on every accrual; the only attacker cost is one burned NFT + gas. The asset lost is the protocol's in-motion / in-conversion yield routed to phlimbo, NOT user principal and NOT an insolvency of SYA (SYA holds no strategy principal; it pulls payment from the claimer). BRICK direction (unconfigured reward token): actualPayment overflows ~1e12x, safeTransferFrom reverts, and every yielding claim fails until the owner configures the token (full availability outage of the sole core function, fail-safe). Capped below High because the attack path is gated by an owner config OMISSION the attacker neither controls nor can induce (C4 'value leak with stated assumptions, but external requirements') and because the asset is in-motion yield (loss-of-yield Medium ceiling).
attackPath: PRECONDITION (benign owner omission, NOT attacker-controllable): owner registers a sub-18-dec strategy token via addYieldStrategy(strategy, USDT) (L227, no decimals arg, no TokenConfig required) and configures the reward token, but omits the separate setTokenConfig(USDT,6,1e18) (L280). USDT stays at the default struct state decimals==0 && normalizedExchangeRate==0.
1. The unconfigured USDT strategy accrues real yield, e.g. 1000 USDT (1000e6 native).
2. Any NFT holder calls claim(nftIndex, minRewardTokenSupplied=0, exemptStrategies=[all other correctly-configured strategies]) to isolate the misconfigured one (exemptStrategies, L473).
3. skimSurplus(USDT, msg.sender) delivers the full 1000e6 USDT to the claimer (L484) — real value received, independent of SYA pricing.
4. _normalizeAmount(1000e6, USDT) hits the fail-open fallback (L591 `return amount;`) and returns 1000e6 treated as 18-dec, so totalNormalizedYield is understated ~1e12x (L489).
5. claimerPayment = 1000e6 * (10000-discount)/10000 (L497); actualPayment = _denormalizeAmount(...) divides by 10**(18-6)=1e12 (L634) => floors to 0 (L498).

6. actualPayment(0) >= minRewardTokenSupplied(0) passes (L501); nudge/phlimbo amounts are 0; safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, this, 0) succeeds (L509). Net: claimer keeps 1000 USDT of real yield for 0 reward token; phlimbo stakers receive nothing. Repeatable every accrual.

BRICK variant: a sub-18-dec reward token left unconfigured makes actualPayment ~1e12x too large, safeTransferFrom (L509) reverts, and every yielding claim fails until the owner configures it (fail-safe outage).
recommendation: Make the unconfigured state FAIL-CLOSED, not fail-open. Any one closes the drain: (1) add an explicit `bool configured` to TokenConfig (set only by setTokenConfig) and revert in _normalizeAmount/_denormalizeAmount (or in claim) when a registered/reward token is unconfigured, instead of assuming 18-dec; (2) require tokenConfigs[token].decimals != 0 (or the configured flag) inside addYieldStrategy AND setRewardToken; (3) fold decimals into addYieldStrategy's signature. Defense-in-depth (also hardens L-01): revert when actualPayment == 0 for non-zero delivered yield. Ship a deploy checklist: every strategy token AND the reward token MUST be configured before claims are enabled. The proposed `configured` flag also resolves PARK-08 (a real 0-decimal token indistinguishable from unconfigured).
verification: PoC-confirmed via Tier-3 invariant property-4 PAYMENT-FLOOR/ZERO-PAYMENT-WITH-YIELD DRAIN (test_DecimalDrain_UnconfiguredStrategyToken_ZeroPayment: a 6-dec strategy token left unconfigured yields the claimer 1000e6 real tokens while actualPayment==0 and phlimbo==0; the control test with the token configured charges the full 1000e6, proving the gap is the missing setTokenConfig) AND by halmos symbolic proof on REAL bytecode: SYMBOLIC-001 refutes 'payment>0' with a concrete counterexample via SYAHarness.exposedDenormalize, SYMBOLIC-002 PROVES the exact zero-payment region (actualPayment==0 <=> totalNormalizedYield*(10000-discountRate)/10000 < 10**(18-rewardTokenDecimals)).

poc.result: 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped. DRAIN: a 6-dec strategy token left UNCONFIGURED yields the claimer 1000e6 real underlying while actualPayment==0, phlimbo==0, SYA retains 0, and calculateClaimAmount previews 0 (no owner signal). CONTROL: the identical scenario WITH the single forgotten setTokenConfig charges the full 1000e6 to the claimer and routes 1000e6 to phlimbo, proving the gap is the one missing setTokenConfig call and not the amount.

severityDispute.highArgument: Insecure-by-default for the dominant token type: the vulnerable state (decimals==0) is the DEFAULT a freshly-registered token has, reached by doing LESS than the under-documented, unenforced full setup, on exactly the 6-dec stablecoins a 'stable yield accumulator' is built for. Impact-on-trigger is unambiguous direct theft: 100% of the strategy's yield, permissionless, repeatable, machine-verified; preview shows 0 so a careful owner gets no signal. Under this reading the config-omission is the EXPECTED deployment, not a mitigating external requirement => Plausible-High.
severityDispute.mediumArgument: The C4 High bar is direct loss OR a valid attack path with NO precondition the attacker cannot satisfy; this bug requires an owner config omission the attacker cannot control or induce. The C4 Medium definition explicitly carves out 'leak value ... with stated assumptions, but external requirements'; the forgotten setTokenConfig IS that. The asset at risk is in-motion yield owed to phlimbo, not principal (loss-of-yield Medium ceiling). No insolvency; the brick variant is fail-safe. Both LLM scanners rated Medium. Direct precedent: phoenix CLASS-001, a PoC-confirmed drain gated on an external condition, held to Medium on the same clause.
severityDispute.resolution: MEDIUM (M-01), at the TOP of the band. The no-precondition slice is empty (no attack against a correctly-configured protocol), so it fails the High bar and lands on the Medium external-requirement definition. The Medium ceiling here is set by the C4 external-requirement criterion, NOT by the Law-3 footgun framing (a footgun CAN be High when it enables direct loss). Remediation is mandatory either way.
severityDispute.dissentForAuditor: DISSENT FLAGGED for severity-auditor. A reasonable judge could rate this Plausible-High on the 'insecure-by-default for the most common (6-dec) token type + direct 100% theft' reading. Classifier verdict is Medium-top-of-band on strict C4 external-requirement text + scanner consensus + loss-of-yield cap + the phoenix CLASS-001 precedent. Please second-opinion the Medium-vs-High call explicitly; the delta does not change remediation urgency.

KI#2 blesses the normalization MATH for CONFIGURED tokens only. KI#4/#5 cover the depeg / discount owner-drain framing (the separate C-01 item, a different root cause). Hazard is the missing enforcement, not the formula.
